rows.source: HSE tyre inflation and wheel safety
rows.verified: Tyre removal, replacement and inflation should only be carried out by competent staff.

rows.source: HSE tyre inflation and wheel safety
rows.verified: Manual-handling injuries account for nearly half of reported tyre-related incidents described by HSE.

rows.source: HSE tyre inflation and wheel safety
rows.verified: Tool-related injuries make up around a quarter of tyre incidents, particularly those involving hand tools such as tyre levers.

rows.source: HSE tyre inflation and wheel safety
rows.verified: Compressed-air failures can rupture tyres or violently separate wheel components, causing serious or fatal injuries.

rows.source: HSE tyre inflation and wheel safety
rows.verified: Inflated tyres contain substantial stored energy determined by inflation pressure and tyre surface area.

rows.source: HSE tyre inflation and wheel safety
rows.verified: The airline between the clip-on chuck and pressure control should be long enough for the operator to stand outside the likely explosion trajectory.

rows.source: HSE tyre inflation and wheel safety
rows.verified: Pressure controls must not be jammed open and unrestricted airlines without a gauge or pressure-control device must not be used.

rows.source: HSE tyre inflation and wheel safety
rows.verified: Hot work must not be carried out on a wheel while a tyre remains fitted because heat can trigger an immediate or delayed explosion.

rows.source: HSE tyre inflation and wheel safety
rows.verified: Tyre risk depends on wheel type, pressure, tyre condition, seating, restraint, inflation equipment, hot-work history and worker competence.

rows.source: HSE tyre inflation and wheel safety
rows.verified: Tyre and wheel evidence is assembly-, pressure-, condition-, task- and operator-specific and is not an exact parcel-level explosion probability.

rows.source: HSE food-and-drink disinfectant controls
rows.verified: Food-and-drink disinfectants are hazardous substances that may harm skin, eyes or the respiratory system and can be harmful if swallowed.

rows.source: HSE food-and-drink disinfectant controls
rows.verified: COSHH assessments should identify every disinfectant, its hazards and the measures used to control operator exposure.

rows.source: HSE food-and-drink disinfectant controls
rows.verified: Assessments should address storage, chemical compatibility, dilution, application, monitoring, health surveillance, training, washing, emergencies and waste disposal.

rows.source: HSE food-and-drink disinfectant controls
rows.verified: Chlorine-based disinfectants can release toxic chlorine gas when mixed with acids or oxidising detergents.

rows.source: HSE food-and-drink disinfectant controls
rows.verified: Peracetic-acid disinfectants can form explosive mixtures with incompatible acid or alkali cleaning products.

rows.source: HSE food-and-drink disinfectant controls
rows.verified: Clean-in-place systems reduce internal plant-disinfection exposure when maintained properly and operated under safe systems of work.

rows.source: HSE food-and-drink disinfectant controls
rows.verified: Fogging generates fine droplets that can stay airborne for 45 to 60 minutes or longer, requiring controlled re-entry arrangements.

rows.source: HSE food-and-drink disinfectant controls
rows.verified: Health surveillance is required where the statutory criteria are met and is particularly relevant to aldehyde exposure or dermatitis risk.

rows.source: HSE food-and-drink disinfectant controls
rows.verified: Disinfectant risk depends on active chemistry, concentration, incompatibilities, application method, aerosol generation, ventilation and re-entry timing.

rows.source: HSE food-and-drink disinfectant controls
rows.verified: Disinfectant evidence is product-, process-, concentration-, exposure- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level poisoning probability.
